stops.note: an ethnic name first recorded in the Orkhon inscriptions of the 730s
after the Mongol invasion of 1241, chroniclers such as Matthew Paris added an 'r', punning on Tartarus, the classical hell
'sauce tartare' and dishes 'à la tartare' were named for the supposedly wild Tatars; the tale that they tenderized meat under their saddles is a legend
'steak tartare' appears on English menus in the early 1900s

current_meaning: finely chopped raw meat or fish, as in steak tartare
